long_biography.plain_text:
Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan has directed the United Arab Emirates' foreign policy since becoming foreign minister in 2006. A political-science graduate of UAE University, he previously worked in federal information and culture roles. He later became Deputy Prime Minister while retaining the foreign-affairs portfolio.

His tenure has widened the country's diplomatic reach and supported new economic partnerships. He also led negotiations to establish diplomatic relations with Israel and signed the Abraham Accords for the UAE in 2020. Beyond formal duties, he is an avid reader and student of history with interests in classical Arab music and scuba diving.
